sentences.text: This animal belongs to the group of polycotylid plesiosaurs, a family of marine reptiles.
Scientists currently recognize only one species within this genus, known from two skulls and some partial skeletons.
It holds the record for being the smallest known member of the polycotylid family.
The main skull specimen measures 44.4 centimeters long, while the secondary skull is 43 centimeters long.
Fully grown adults reached a total length of approximately 2.3 to 2.6 meters.
The upper jaw contained at least 26 teeth used for catching prey.
The skull features unusually large eye sockets, a trait often seen in young animals.
The name honors Unhcegila, a Lakota legend describing a horned water serpent with keen eyes.
The specific name specta refers to hypothesized visual adaptations linked to those large eye sockets.
Clark, O'Keefe, and Slack formally described the genus and species Unktaheela specta in 2023.
The primary specimen, cataloged as UCM 35059, was found near Redbird in Niobrara County, Wyoming.
A secondary specimen, SDSM 142501, was discovered on the Thomas Conger Ranch near Buffalo Gap in South Dakota.
Kenneth Carpenter initially identified the main skull as a juvenile Dolichorhynchops osborni in 1996.
Many bones in the specimens are fused, proving the animals were fully grown despite their juvenile-looking heads.
Wide upper arm bones distinguish this species from the narrow arm bones of young plesiosaurs.
Phylogenetic analysis places this genus within the plesiosaur clade Leptocleidia.
It forms a specific group called Dolichorhynchia alongside species of Dolichorhynchops within the Polycotylinae.
Fossils originate from the Late Cretaceous Sharon Springs Formation in the United States.
This animal lived during the Campanian stage, between 83.6 and 72.2 million years ago.
It is debated whether the juvenile-like features represent true growth stages or are unique adult characteristics.
